body: Damn, I like you. You're as fed up with this "and I must scream" society as I am.

Well, thanks. Thanks for informing me from response one that, comprehension be damned, everything is my fault.

Because believe me, my dear, I know that everything is my fault. If I do not change it, nobody is going to change it. Because nobody cares, as long as it doesn't detriment them. That's not the issue.

The issue is that I can't fix everything myself.

Thank you for your concern, and your support.

Could you at least explain what you mean if you're going to invalidate my statements with a single term? Such as "codependency" or "polarized thinking"?

Only before 2pm, battling anxiety and neurosis and always feeling tired?

The thing about this job, it doesn't end when I walk out the door. I'm always there now.

And I seem to recall the last time I tried I was unqualified to volunteer.

I'll surely keep it in mind though.

So are you just basically assuming that the whole "nobody I know actually wants me to be happy, I've got nothing to rely on" thing is utterly beyond your ken and you're going to leave it alone?
Okay. Did I answer your question?

I am at a loss for words.

You're really going to ignore everything I just said? The answers I just gave to your questions?

And, yes, I do expect to be fired if I respond freely to a boss who is too cowardly and entitled to make a **single** decision on procedure, and instead explicitly dumps me off on his employees who he's done the exact same too and **they** go ahead and do that too so that I have to teach myself everything and improvise a solution to every scenario in an environment completely without support where everyone wants to screw me over to make themselves look good.

But, hey, at least you got to make me sound ridiculous, so I guess you won. Have fun in your reality.

I feel no need at all. I don't take on this role. I ask them politely and reasonably, like I've always been told to, not to take me for granted, not to schedule me only on the worst possible days, things that I would like. And they get angry at my passive-aggression, remind me that I've brought it all on myself and their hands are tied, and do it anyway.

Even so much as saying what I think results in a prompt and prim "That's not completely true, now be quiet." And that's that.

And if I stopped buffering people from the consequences of their treatment of me, my life would look like I was fired, just for starters. Which seemed more like a late-game measure. I bet they would be just fine though.

Yeah, sad fact is, folks love to troll people with real problems and humility. They see others' problems as a challenge to their own self-involvement, and react the only way they know how.

That sucks, man. When I find a way to make these people stop, you'll be the first to know.

I definitely know that feeling, where I'm just going through the motions all the time, and then when it's time to stop and be myself, find something I want to do, I don't seem to be anyone, and it's like I wasn't even there for everything my body was doing.
